Riva Romance, who finished second to him that day, won at Orange nine days later when a short-priced favorite. Lees has been patient with High Power, trialling him twice in May but not racing him as a two-year-old. He then gave him three trials in August and September to fit him for his first-up assignment.    “High Power has trained on really well since his first race,” Lees said. “The 1400m looks ideal, and I’m expecting him to be hard to beat.”    Lees, however, won’t be rushing the youngster to Melbourne for the latter part of the spring carnival, explaining that has come too quick for him. He is also confident another Avdulla mount, Greater Good, will run well in the Sydney Polo Club Provincial & Country Maiden Plate (1300m).    Lees has withdrawn his third Hawkesbury acceptor, Seeblume (Glyn Schofield), from the Coca Cola Amatil Class 1 Handicap (1400m).    Avdulla, the current Hawkesbury premiership pacesetter, has an excellent book of six rides (three of them are favorites and another second favorite). He also partners Eleazar (XI FIP World Polo Championship Maiden, 1000m) for Team Hawkes, Metamorphic (Nestle Maiden, 1300m) and Sansa (Lion Maiden Plate, 1500m) for Chris Waller, and Organza (Coca Cola Amatil F&M Class 1, 1400m) for James Cummings.    Metamorphic, placed at all four starts (three of them in town), resumes as a gelding. He hasn’t started since finishing third as an odds-on favorite on the Beaumont track in late July.    The rail is in the TRUE position for tomorrow’s meeting, and a “Soft 6” rating was posted early this morning. The penetrometer reading was 5.22. Hawkesbury has received 41mm of rain (none in the last 24 hours) in the past week, and 8mm of irrigation (again none in the last 24 hours) has been put on the track. text: “She gets a bit of pressure in her heels and the bar plates just help her. They are nearly as light as normal plates and they tend to help her more than hinder.

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: Racing NSW Stewards today handed down their findings in respect to charges issued against former Managing Director of Godolphin Australia Mr Henry Plumptre and Licensed Trainer Mr John O’Shea relative to an inquiry opened on 27 June 2017, in respect to the racehorse Polemic being infected with the notifiable disease or condition strangles in August 2016. Barrister Mr Matthew Stirling assisted Mr O’Shea and Barrister Mr Peter Braham SC assisted Mr Plumptre and represented the interests of Godolphin Australia. Final written submission were received from Mr Stirling, on behalf of Mr O’Shea, on 11 August 2017.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: Mr Plumptre – Penalty Consideration  Mr Plumptre pleaded guilty to a charge under AR64K(2), in that he did not report as soon as possible by the quickest means of communication available to Racing NSW, the Principal Racing Authority in NSW, that the racehorse Polemic was confirmed as being infected with the notifiable disease or condition strangles as required by AR64K(2) when he became aware that the racehorse Polemic was so infected, on 5 August 2016.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: In consideration of penalty, the relevant factors taken into account by the Stewards included, but are not limited to, the following:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 1. The guilty plea entered at the first available opportunity and the assistance Mr Plumptre provided during the inquiry. This included Mr Plumptre recognising that his conduct in the circumstances was wrong and not in keeping with the high standards set by the industry.  2. Mr Plumptre is of good character and has no previous history of such conduct. There were a number of impressive references submitted testifying to Mr Plumptre’s contribution to the thoroughbred industry and good character.  3. Contrition shown by Mr Plumptre  4. Objective seriousness of the offence and potential ramifications of not reporting the disease or condition. In this respect, the Stewards were satisfied that appropriate bio-security measures were put in place to prevent the disease being transferred to other horses.  5. Precedent penalties under the Rules of Racing.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: The Stewards feel it important to make comment in respect to the precedent in the decision of the Victorian Racing Appeals and Disciplinary Board, constituted by Judge Bowman, in the case of Racing Victoria Stewards and Matthew Cumani 16 May 2017 whereby Mr Cumani’s trainers licence was suspended for a period of 11 weeks in addition to a fine of $20,000. The Stewards identify several distinguishing features of the Cumani case as compared to the offence of Mr Plumptre, noting that there are also a number of common issues in both.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: The Racing NSW Stewards determined that, due to the distinguishing features of Mr Cumani’s case that the appropriate penalty issued to Mr Plumptre be a fine rather than a period of disqualification. The Stewards have also considered the fact that Godolphin Australia is one of the major racing operations in Australia and there is an expectation that the Godolphin Australia operates a highest possible standards and to promote compliance with the Rules of Racing.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: Further, the Racing NSW Stewards have had regard to the Reasons for Decision of the NSW Racing Appeals Tribunal, constituted by Mr D Amarti, in the 2014 appeal by NSW licensed trainer, Darren Smith:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 6. To the extent that criminal law principles such as deterrence are considered, they are not relevant. To the extent that proportionality of sentencing is said to be considered, it is not relevant. In respect of the first of those, the Tribunal in determining what order is appropriate has regard to what message is to be given to this individual trainer to ensure that in the future this type of conduct is not repeated, but to ensure that there is an appropriate penalty imposed to indicate the response of the community to integrity and welfare issues. In addition, it is a question of what general message is required to be sent to the community at large to indicate to those who might be like-minded to engage in such conduct, what the likely consequences are, and, secondly, to indicate to the broader community who are not likely to engage in the type of conduct that, should it be detected, they, whether they be wagerers or people just generally interested in the individual code, will know that it is operating at the highest possible standards.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: And also to the Reasons for Decision of the Racing NSW Appeal Panel, chaired by Mr T Hale SC, in the 2017 appeal by NSW licensed trainer, Con Karakatsanis:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 43. In our view, by analogy these principles concerning deterrence are apposite to determining penalty for breach of the rules of racing. It will be noted that in Foreman the role of deterrence was considered in relation to the protection of the public. Deterrence will have a broader application in relation to the rules of racing. The principles will extend not only to the protection of the public but also the promotion of the safety or horses and jockeys as well as the integrity of racing. In determining penalty, consideration may be given to the deterrent effect that the penalty might achieve in deterring a repetition of the offence and in deterring others who might be tempted to fall short of the high standards required of them under the rules of racing. The penalty may also be seen as publicly marking the seriousness of the offence.”

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: Accordingly, after consideration of the above matters, the Stewards have determined that the appropriate penalty for the offence is a $20,000 fine. Having regard to Mr Plumptre’s co-operation with the Stewards and his guilty plea entered at the first available opportunity, the Stewards determine that Mr Plumptre is entitled to a 25% reduction of that penalty and accordingly issue Mr Plumptre with a fine of $15,000.

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 1. A number of email and phone records were tendered at the Stewards inquiry. These records establish the following factual matters  a. The evidence establishes that there was an email group including Godolphin employees Mr O’Shea, Dr Robson, Dr Adams and Mr Reid (Email Group), that received emails from Vetnostics providing the results of blood and swab samples taken from Godolphin horses.  b. On 2 August 2016, Dr Adams took a swab sample from the submandibular swelling of Polemic and submitted it to Vetnostics for analysis for strangles.  c. At 10:12am or 10.16am (noted as 10.12am in the recipient’s inbox but 10.16am on the email) on 4 August 2016, the Email Group received an email from Vetnostics reporting that the results of the interim culture were that Polemic had tested positive to Beta-haem. Streptococcus.  d. At or around 1:41pm or 1.46pm (noted as 1.41pm in the recipient’s inbox but 1.46pm on the email) on 4 August 2016, the Email Group received a further email from Vetnostics reporting that the results of the interim culture were that Polemic had tested positive to Strep. equi subsp. equi (strangles).  e. At 10:41am on 5 August 2016, the Email Group received a further email from Vetnostics reporting that the results of the final culture were that Polemic had tested positive to strangles.  f. The evidence establishes that Mr O’Shea received and accessed the emails as detailed in paragraphs c. to e., however Mr O’Shea advised he did not read these emails as Polemic was not in the racing population. There is no evidence before the Stewards that establishes Mr O’Shea read the said emails.  g. On 4 August 2016, the mobile phone records of Godolphin veterinarian’s Dr Trevor Robson and Dr Graeme Adams show that that the vets communicated soon after the emails listed in paragraphs c. and d. were received.  In particular:  i. at 10:58am (being a little over 40 minutes after receipt of the email detailed in paragraph c. above), Dr Adams called Dr Robson with a call duration of 2 seconds (which suggests that the call did not go through);  ii. at 11:04am (being 6 minutes later), Dr Adams again called Dr Robson and they spoke for 7 minutes, 52 seconds;  iii.  at 1:56pm (being 10 minutes after receipt of the email detailed in paragraph d. above), Dr Adams again called Dr Robson with a call duration of 3 seconds (which suggests that the call did not go through); and  iv. at 2:09pm (being 13 minutes later), Dr Robson called Dr Adams (which suggests he returned Dr Adams call) and they spoke for 16 minutes, 49 seconds.  h. The mobile phone records of Dr Robson establish he was present at Warwick Farm on 4 August 2016, between 3:34pm and 5:50pm and in the Agnes Banks region on the morning of 5 August 2016.  i. The mobile phone records of Mr O’Shea establish he was at Warwick Farm on the afternoon of 4 August 2016 and at Agnes Banks on the morning of 5 August 2016.

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 14. Mr Stirling’s submissions, on behalf of Mr O’Shea, state that Mr O’Shea should not be found guilty of the charge for being a party to Mr Plumptre’s breach of AR64K for the following reasons

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: a. Mr Plumptre has not stated in his evidence that Mr O’Shea “advised [him] not to report the disease or condition;  b. A finding that Mr O’Shea was a party to Mr Plumptre’s breach is completely inconsistent with Mr Plumptre’s signed testimony;  c. Mr O’Shea denies giving the advice;  d. Mr O’Shea has a longstanding record of good character;  e. When faced with the same circumstances in 2008 the matter was reported to Racing NSW;  f. Dr Robson’s evidence does not establish that Mr O’Shea directly asked Mr Plumptre not to report the matter;  g. The charge is inconsistent with Mr Reid’s evidence;  h. Absence of proof that Mr Plumptre’s decision not to report was influenced by Mr O’Shea;  i. The Stewards case is inconsistent with the positons of employment that Mr Plumptre and Mr O’Shea held at Godolphin Australia.

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 15. Mr Stirling’s submissions, on behalf of Mr O’Shea, state that Mr O’Shea should not be found guilty of the charge of providing false and/or misleading evidence for the following reasons;  a. The High Court authority of Smith v NSW Bar Association (1992) 176 CLR 256 at [39] which states it is inappropriate to make findings a person has deliberately lied on the single oath of another man and without the strongest circumstantial evidence;  b. The charge relates to conversations that took place over a year ago;  c. Dr Robson is a problematic witness;  d. The evidence of Mr Plumptre does not support a guilty finding;  e. Mr Reid conceded that he was not really part of the group conversation on 5 August 2016;  f. Mr O’Shea’s version of events is equally plausible;  g. Mr O’Shea is supported by his 20-year long record as a trainer of integrity;  h. Mr O’Shea had no motivation to lie;  i. The rejection of his evidence is different to a finding of false evidence;  j. Inherit inconsistency in the Stewards case, in that although he [Mr O’Shea] thought Polemic had strangles, he is lying to the Stewards when he says he did not know Polemic had strangles and  k. No reason to reject Dr Adams evidence.

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 16. The Stewards find that Dr Robson was unrelenting in his evidence in respect to advice he received from Dr Adams that Polemic had tested positive to strangles prior to the conversation with Mr O’Shea on 4 August 2016 and the meeting on 5 August 2016. This evidence was given prior to additional evidence being presented to the Stewards, which, as detailed above, confirmed that the initial positive strangles advice was originally emailed to the Godolphin Email Group on 4 August 2016 and not the 5 August 2016 as the initial evidence originally suggested. Further having regard to the phone and email evidence, the Stewards accept Dr Robson’s evidence that he advised Mr O’Shea that Polemic had tested positive to strangles and that Mr O’Shea told Dr Robson that he didn’t want to report the matter to Racing NSW.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 17. The Stewards find that at this point in time Mr O’Shea should have reported the positive test result immediately to Mr Plumptre.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 18. The Stewards find that on the morning of 5 August 2016, a group discussion (5 August Group Discussion) took place at Osborne Park Agnes Banks in respect to the Polemic positive test result. The evidence of Dr Robson is that Mr O’Shea “stated why he didn’t want Henry [Plumptre] to tell the Stewards.”
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 19. Further the evidence of Mr Plumptre in respect to the 5 August 2016 Group Discussion at Osborne park was that “he [Mr O’Shea] was fairly blunt about what we needed to do” and that “it was likely that there was going to be a shutdown and that was probably the prime driver for their reluctance or John’s reluctance to say anything about it.” The Stewards find that these statements from Mr Plumptre should be viewed as meaning that Mr O’Shea advised Mr Plumptre not to report the strangles positive.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 20. Having considered all the evidence and submissions, the Stewards find Mr O’Shea guilty of the charge issued under AR175(l).
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 21. The Stewards find that on two occasions, firstly on the afternoon of 4 August 2016 and secondly on the morning of 5 August 2016, Mr O’Shea was advised by Dr Robson that Polemic had tested positive to strangles. In making these findings the Stewards accept the evidence of Dr Robson, Mr Plumptre and Mr Reid having regard to Mr Stirlings submissions in respect to the High Court decision in Smith (as referred to above) and R v Hook (1858), Dears. & Bell 606 at 42.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 22. Further, the Stewards have considered the submissions made in respect to Smith (as referred to above) which held at [37] that:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: “There is a difference between the rejection of a person’s evidence and finding that he or she deliberately lied….as a matter of logic and common sense, something more than a rejection of a person’s evidence is necessary before there can be a finding that he or she deliberately lied in giving of the evidence”
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Godolphin Strangles Hearing - Stewards Findings
text: 23. After considering all the evidence and submissions, the Stewards are satisfied to the requisite standard, the Briginshaw standard, that when Mr O’Shea provided the evidence particularised in the charge, that he gave such evidence in the knowledge that it was false and/or misleading.  In arriving at that finding, the Stewards are of the view that it is not a case of the oath of a single man but the evidence of Dr Robson, Mr Reid and Mr Plumptre as to the purpose and substance of the 5 August Group Discussion, and the phone and email records as to the positive results that had been received the previous day. Accordingly, the Stewards find Mr O’Shea guilty of the charge under AR175(g).

text: 3. It was also submitted on behalf of Mr Paul Murray that cobalt was not a prohibited substance at the relevant time as it predated the introduction of the threshold in the Australian Rules of Racing on 1 January 2015.  In making that submission, Mr O’Neill submitted that the contrary findings of the Racing Appeals Tribunal in the case of Darren Smith (delivered on 22 July 2014) were inconsistent with the NSW Court of Appeal decision in Day v Harness Racing NSW [2014] NSWCA 423.  The Stewards reject that submission and note that the Racing Appeals Tribunal considered the NSW Court of Appeal decision in Day v Harness Racing NSW at some length in arriving at its finding that cobalt was a prohibited substance prior to the introduction of the threshold. The Stewards further note that the submission is not supported by AR178C(1) which exempts cobalt from being a prohibited substance under AR178B if present at concentrations at or below the threshold rather than deeming it to be a prohibited substance if above the threshold. text: 4. In respect of the administration charges under AR175(h)(i) and AR175(h)(ii), the Stewards make the finding that Mr Paul Murray administered a prohibited substance, namely cobalt, to Alma’s Fury.  As to the more serious of the charges, being AR175(h)(i), the Stewards also find that Mr Paul Murray did so “for the purpose of affecting the performance” of Alma’s Fury in a race.  In this respect, the Stewards note the statement by the Racing Appeals Tribunal at paragraph 9 of its penalty findings in the matter of Darren Smith (delivered on 22 July 2014) that “Why else would there have been an administration of cobalt if it was not done in the belief that it would provide a benefit to the horse? It is the intent, not the actual effect, to which the rules are directed”.  The Stewards also note the finding by the Racing NSW Appeal Panel in the Appeals of Mr Sam Kavanagh, Dr Tom Brennan and Dr Adam Matthews (delivered on 6 May 2016) at paragraphs 77 and 78 that administration with the intent of aiding the recovery of a horse is for the purpose of assisting its performance in a race.  In making those findings, the Stewards note that evidence of Mr Paul Murray varied in respect of his knowledge of the existence of the bottle discovered in his fridge on 17 June 2014 and further note that he admitted to administering a substance from a similar bottle that gave no indication of who manufactured it, what its precise ingredients were or where it came from.

title: Stewards Footage Of Upheld Protest At Goulburn
text: Prior to the declaration of correct weight and after viewing a replay of the race, Mr Chris Polglase, Deputy Chief Steward SERA, lodged an objection on behalf of the connections of runner-up  Fallada and in the public interest, against Read All About It being declared the winner on the grounds Read All About It had caused interference to Fallada passing the 100m.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Footage Of Upheld Protest At Goulburn
text: Mr Polglase took no further part in the hearing and the remaining panel members considered the merit of the objection. On the evidence, it was established that passing the 100m Read All About It shifted out and made contact with Fallada which was inconvenienced and taken out. Bearing in mind that in the lead up to the incident Fallada was also making ground on Read All About It and that as a consequence of the interference, Fallada lost momentum but then recommenced to make ground on Read All About It in the run to the line, and also taking into account the margin of only a nose between the respective runners, Stewards were satisfied that had the interference not occurred that Fallada would have finished ahead of Read All About It and, as such, upheld the objection.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Footage Of Upheld Protest At Goulburn
text: Stewards amended the placings to read 1st: Fallada; 2nd Read All About It; 3rd Texacody and 4th Talladega Knight and declared correct weight.

text: At a subsequent inquiry, Fallada’s rider Shaun Guymer was spoken to, and told that he must be more aware of interference during a race that presented the opportunity of at least viewing a replay of the race to determine whether there were grounds to lodge an objection on behalf of connections.

title: Stewards Report - Chautauqua
text: The behaviourist who has been educating Chautauqua to jump from the barriers advised Stewards that he had been working with the gelding since on or around 1 August 2018. He said in that period of time, whilst Chautauqua had not jumped satisfactorily in official trials, the gelding had improved by jumping from the barriers, whereas previously Chautauqua had refused to begin. He indicated to the Stewards that in his opinion, with further education and being encouraged by the gelding beginning well in jump outs, he was confident he could encourage gelding to begin in a competitive manner. title: Stewards Inquiry - The Lion
text: Racing NSW Stewards conducted an inquiry into the Analysts’ findings of 4 hydroxy xylazine in a post-race urine sample taken from The Lion following the gelding winning Race 2 – TAB Highway Handicap conducted at Randwick on 9 June 2018.

title: Stewards Inquiry - The Lion
text: Evidence was taken from the trainer of The Lion Ms Michelle Fleming, who as managing owner represented the interests of the owners, Mr B McHugh Part Owner of the gelding, Racing NSW Official Veterinarian Dr James Mizzi and ARFL General Manager Mr John Keledjian. The Stewards established the following;
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Inquiry - The Lion
text: 1. On Sunday 3 June 2018 Ms Fleming administered a substance containing 3ml xylazine (containing 300mg of xylazine hydrochloride) and 3ml A.C.P to facilitate the clipping of the gelding. 2. The substance was sourced from another trainer who had obtained the product from her veterinarian. 3. Ms Fleming did not obtain any veterinary advice prior to administering the substance. 4. The dosage administered to The Lion according to Dr Mizzi was greater than the recommended dosage to relax a horse for clipping. 5. The level of 4 hydroxy xylazine detected in the sample by the Australian Racing Forensic Laboratory was low.

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: On Thursday, 23rd May 2019, an inquiry was opened into the circumstances surrounding the death on the evening of Sunday, 24th February 2019 of I Am Rocky, a 4YO bay entire, whilst it was in the care of the Joseph Jones Racing Partnership, and also into the care that the horse was afforded in the lead up to its death.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: Evidence was taken from the co-trainers of the training partnership consisting of Mrs Barbara Joseph, Mr Paul Jones and Mr Matt Jones, and stable foreperson Mr S. Jamieson, stablehand Ms L. Fehre, registered owner of I Am Rocky, Mr C. Warne, Dr J. Laing – Bungendore Veterinary Surgery and Dr Toby Koenig – Chief Veterinary Officer RNSW. Ms L. Hours attended the inquiry as a support person for Mr Warne.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: The inquiry was continued today with further evidence being taken from Mrs B. Joseph, Mr P. Jones, Mr M. Jones, Mr C. Warne, Dr J. Laing and Dr T. Koenig. Ms L. Hours again attended the inquiry as a support person for Mr Warne but also provided evidence.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: Mrs B. Joseph, Mr P. Jones and Mr M. Jones pleaded guilty to the following two charges:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: Charge 1
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: Under AR103(4) that they did fail to lodge a stable return for the four-year-old horse I Am Rocky, which after joining the Joseph Jones Racing stables, had been in active work for a period of approximately nine weeks.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: Charge 2
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: Under AR231(1)(b)(iii) that they did fail to provide for veterinary treatment where such treatment was necessary as:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (1) They were at all relevant times the co-trainers of the four-year-old entire I Am Rocky.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (2) In accordance with AR98(2), they are persons training in partnership and as such share all responsibilities, obligations and rights under the Rules in relation to training horses.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (3) Under LR78(2), they were, during the relevant times, responsible for the care, control and supervision of I Am Rocky.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (4) At approximately 4am on Saturday, 23 February 2019, co-trainer Mr M. Jones became aware that I Am Rocky was displaying symptoms of colic.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (5) At approximately 8:09am on Saturday, 23 February 2019, Mr P. Jones became aware that I Am Rocky was again displaying symptoms of colic.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (6) That during Saturday, 23 February 2019, stable foreperson Mr S. Jamieson had observed that I Am Rocky had “been lethargic all day”.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (7) That during Saturday, 23 February 2019, they did fail to provide for veterinary treatment of I Am Rocky when the horse was displaying symptoms of colic and such treatment was necessary for the horse.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (8) That after observing that I Am Rocky was dull and lethargic in its stable at approximately 7am on Sunday, 24 February 2019, licensed stablehand Ms L. Fehre contacted Mr S. Jamieson soon after and reported to him words to the effect “He looks unwell and he probably needs a vet”.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (9) That at no time did they, subsequent to Saturday, 23 February 2019 and whilst I Am Rocky remained in their care, control and supervision at their registered racing stables provide for veterinary treatment of the horse, when such treatment was necessary for the horse.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (10) I Am Rocky was found deceased in its stable at approximately 7:30pm on Sunday, 24 February 2019 by stable foreperson Mr S. Jamieson.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Fine And Suspend Jones Training Partnership
text: (11) A post-mortem examination report completed by Dr S. Raidal, Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory (Charles Sturt University), on 26 February 2019, provided a gross diagnosis of right dorsal displacement of the large colon, likely secondary to diffuse typhlocolitis ultimately was the cause of the death of I Am Rocky. The Report also identified and described numerous superficial wounds and subcutaneous haemorrhages, consistent with trauma following an episode of uncontrolled colic pain.

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: Racing NSW Stewards continued an inquiry that was opened at Royal Randwick on Saturday, 4 March 2023 in relation to Nash Rawiller’s riding of Another Cognac in Race 5, Tokyo City Keiba Fireball Stakes.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: Evidence was taken from N Rawiller and trainer of Another Cognac Mr Bryce Heys.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: Stewards considered a written report from Mr Harrison Smithers, Racing New South Form & Betting Analyst, in relation to the wagering activity on the race which did not reveal any integrity concerns.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: Stewards scrutinized the ride of N Rawiller in the home straight, particularly between the 300m and 200m and whether there was an opportunity for him to have directed Another Cognac to the outside of runners into clear running sooner than he did.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: Stewards accepted the evidence of N Rawiller that in discussion with the connections of Another Cognac prior to the race they had agreed with his intention to seek runs closer to the inside as he felt that the horses racing towards the inside were being advantaged on that day.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: N Rawiller gave further evidence that after initially intending to improve into an available run between Midnight In Tokyo and Nipotino in the early part of the straight he then had to identify another option to improve when Midnight In Tokyo commenced to shift away from the running rail near the 300m.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: When questioned specifically whether he should have at this stage of the race immediately shifted across the heels of Nipotino in an endeavor to improve, N Rawiller stated that near the 250m when K McEvoy, the rider of Nipotino, commenced to shift out from behind Economics to follow Dashing Legend he briefly identified an opportunity may exist to improve into the run that was vacated by Nipotino.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: He said however, a short distance later Midnight In Tokyo continued to shift out which closed this run at which stage he then commenced to direct Another Cognac out across the heels of both Nipotino and Willinga Beast from near the 200m with Another Cognac able to be fully tested from near the 150m.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: N Rawiller was advised that whilst his riding between the 300m and 200m was of concern to Stewards, having regard to all of the evidence, they could not be comfortably satisfied that his riding was blameworthy to the extent that he should be charged with a breach of AR129(2) for having failed to take all reasonable and permissible measures to ensure his mount was given full opportunity to gain the best possible place in the field.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Licensed Jockey Nash Rawiller's Ride
text: N Rawiller was, however, told to ensure that he rides his mounts with the necessary purpose and vigor and to endeavor to improve his position at the earliest opportunity, regardless of any preconceived views he may have as to where the best going exists.

text: Racing NSW Stewards today conducted an inquiry into the analyst's finding of caffeine, theophylline, paraxanthine and theobromine being detected in a blood sample taken from Injair after it won Race 4 (Super Maiden Handicap, 1280m) at the Gilgandra race meeting on 5 January 2025.

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: Evidence today was taken from Mr Gavin Groth, the trainer of Injair, Racing NSW Veterinary Officer Dr Rose Bensley and ARFL General Manager Mr John Keledjian. Stewards also considered a brief of evidence provided by Racing NSW Investigators.

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: Background
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: The Stewards established the following:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: On 26 February 2025, Racing NSW Officials notified Mr Groth of the irregularity the sample had returned to caffeine and its metabolites. During the associated stable inspection officials took possession of stable treatment records and examined various medications and feed supplements contained within the stable.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: It was established that in the relevant period Mr Groth had been providing the feed supplement Metabolize to several horses under his care, including Injair.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: Racing NSW Stewards had, at the time of the stable inspection, become aware through liaison with other racing jurisdictions in Australia that the feed supplement Metabolize, which is manufactured by Poseidon Animal Health, had recently been linked to the detection of caffeine in those jurisdictions.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: Samples of Metabolize associated with a case in another jurisdiction had been analysed by the Australian Racing Forensic Laboratory and were found to contain high levels of caffeine.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: A notice was subsequently issued by Racing NSW Stewards to all licensed trainers in NSW warning of the identified link between the detection of caffeine in samples with the use of the feed supplement Metabolize.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: At the inquiry, evidence was tendered from Mr Peter Lord of Poseidon Animal Health that the natural extracts that make up Metabolize do not contain caffeine, however, it had been found that traces of caffeine had been detected in certain batches of the product manufactured in November 2024. Following a quality control process undertaken by the company, it was identified that the contamination had occurred in the supply of one of the raw materials in the powdered blend and that measures had since been put in place to address the issue.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

text: Charge

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: Mr Groth pleaded guilty to the following offence.

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: AR240(2) – Presenting a horse to race with a prohibited substance detected

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: The details of the charge being that he did present Injair to race in the Super Maiden Handicap at the Gilgandra race meeting on 5 January 2025 and a post-race blood sample taken from Injair was found to contain the prohibited substances caffeine, theophylline, paraxanthine and theobromine.

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: In deciding to issue no penalty against Mr Groth in relation to the aforementioned breach of AR240(2), consideration was given to the following circumstances:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: That on the evidence, Stewards were satisfied that the source of the detection of caffeine and its metabolites in the sample obtained from Injair resulted from the ingestion of Metabolize which contained caffeine as a consequence of contamination during production.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: Prior to using Metabolize in his racing stable, Mr Groth had made appropriate inquiries through a reputable veterinary practice relating to horses under his care, following which the use of this product had been proposed.

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: Mr Groth used Metabolize on the basis that he was aware of other trainers having used the product without issue.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Report - Swab Inquiry Relating To Caffeine
text: The product labelling observed by Mr Groth, contained no claims in relation the product treating a disease, condition or injury which would require it to be registered with the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicine Authority (APVMA) as required under AR252.

text: Racing NSW Stewards today conducted an inquiry into the bona-fides of the training of racehorses located at 15 Stroud Avenue Warwick Farm following an investigation being conducted by the Stewards at Warwick Farm racecourse on 17 July 2018. Evidence today was taken from licensed trainer Mr J Austin, licensed stablehand Mr N Auld and Owner Mr S Farah. The Stewards found through an arrangement made between Mr Austin and Lionheart Thoroughbreds, the directors being Mr Auld and Mr Farah, Mr Austin agreed to train a number of racehorses being prepared for the Inglis Ready 2 Race sales to be conducted in October 2018. Due to Mr Austin not having sufficient stables, Mr Austin arranged for the lease of stables located at 15 Stroud Avenue Warwick Farm, where the colts in training for the sale were stabled.

text: Racing NSW Stewards today conducted an inquiry into the circumstances of the death of the racehorse Leshem at Armidale Racecourse on 8 July 2020.

title: Stewards Inquiry Into Death Of Racehorse Leshem
text: Evidence today was taken from Licensed trainer Mr Mark Ostini, the Trainer of Leshem, Licensed Stablehand Mr Mitchell Faulkner, Dr R Bensley, Racing NSW Official Veterinarian / Welfare Officer and Australian Racing Forensic Laboratory Science Manager, Dr A Cawley, via teleconference.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Inquiry Into Death Of Racehorse Leshem
text: Mr M Ostini pleaded guilty to a charge under AR228 (b) of improper conduct in that on the 8 July 2020, he did authorise Mr M Faulkner to administer an intravenous drip which contained multiple substances from a sachet to the racehorse Leshem, which was engaged to race at Scone 0n 10 July 2020, and during the course of administration had added to it the product Pentosan to the drip, which was contrary to labelled and advertised instruction. Such administration being capable of being detrimental to the welfare of the horse and was administered without taking veterinary advice, resulting in Leshem suffering an anaphylactic reaction during the course of administration and Leshem dying whilst being administered the drip.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Inquiry Into Death Of Racehorse Leshem
text: Further Mr M Ostini pleaded guilty to a charge under AR252(1), in that on the 8 July 2020 and days subsequent, he did have in his possession the product Arthropen Vet 250, which was not prescribed to him by a veterinarian for use in his stable or any horse in his care, which is a breach of relevant legislation.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Inquiry Into Death Of Racehorse Leshem
text: Considering all the circumstance relevant to penalty in relation to the charge under AR228 (b), a penalty of 18 months disqualification was applied before allowing mitigation to acknowledge Mr Ostini’s guilty plea and his unblemished disciplinary record established over 20 years, which resulted in that penalty being reduced to a period of 12 months.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Inquiry Into Death Of Racehorse Leshem
text: Accordingly, Mr Ostini was disqualified for a period to commence immediately and expire 16 September 2021. Mr Ostini was told that he was allowed seven (7) days to make appropriate arrangements for the care and relocation of horses in his care and advised of his rights of appeal.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Inquiry Into Death Of Racehorse Leshem
text: Considering all the circumstances relevant to penalty in relation to the charge under AR252(1), including Mr Ostini’s guilty plea and his unblemished disciplinary record established over 20 years, Mr Ostini was disqualified for 3 months to be served concurrently with the penalty applied under AR228 (b).

title: Stewards Inquiry Into Death Of Racehorse Leshem

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: Racing NSW Stewards today resumed an inquiry into Nash Rawiller’s riding of Jailbreak in race 4 (Exceedence New to Vinery Handicap, 1250m) at the Kensington race meeting on Wednesday, 30 September 2020.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: Of concern to the Stewards was Nash Rawiller’s riding of the gelding in the home straight and whether there was an opportunity to take advantage of a run that developed between Xanthus and Avadane for a short distance after entering the home straight and again leaving the 250m.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: Jailbreak raced in a position trailing Xanthus until a point approaching the 150m at which point it had to be steadied after being disappointed for a run between Xanthus and Mission River when both horses shifted ground.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: Nash Rawiller explained that shortly after leaving the 400m he observed that a narrow run had developed between Xanthus and Avadane, however, at this stage of the race he was content to continue to trail the favoured runner Xanthus as it had made ground on the leader Avadane and was racing on terms with that runner in the early stages of the straight.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: He added that at the same point a run had commenced to develop to the outside of Xanthus due to Mission River hanging out and he believed that this run would continue to widen, and with Mission River weakening, he would be able to move that runner wider to secure clear running later in the straight if he had need to do so.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: Nash Rawiller further stated that leaving the 250m when a run was available between Xanthus and Avadane, he observed Xanthus shift in and he therefore attempted a run between Xanthus and Mission River that had developed due to this shift, however, was disappointed for that run when Xanthus shifted back out.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: After considering the explanations provided by jockey Nash Rawiller, he was informed that the explanation provided for remaining to race behind Xanthus leaving the 400m was accepted on the basis that it was a narrow run between Xanthus and Avadane and any amount of movement from either runner would result in Jailbreak having to be checked as it was not positioned to resist a shift from either runner as Xanthus and Avadane were racing on terms in advance of Jailbreak at that stage.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: However, he was advised that in the opinion of the Stewards he had made an error of judgement by not positioning Jailbreak into a run to the inside of Xanthus and outside Avadane leaving the 250m when that run was available.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Jailbreak Inquiry (Nash Rawiller)
text: In determining that this error was not blameworthy, Stewards had regard to the fact that a run did develop to the outside of Xanthus and to the inside of Mission River for a short distance leaving that point and the positioning of Mission River, being back and to the outside of Xanthus would have made it easier for Jailbreak to resist slight movement from either runner as Jailbreak had nearly advanced to be on terms with Mission River.

title: Additonal Stewards Comments - Rosehill (Saturday)
text: Shortly after the start was crowded. From a wide barrier was then shifted behind runners in the early stages. When questioned regarding his riding rounding the home turn and in the early part of the straight and as to whether there was an opportunity to shift to the outside in an endeavour to obtain clear running, rider B Loy stated that upon entering the home straight, Butch’N’Bugs shifted out and away from the rail and he was of the view that Butch’N’Bugs would continue to shift out and take advantage of runs that presented which would have denied him the opportunity of obtaining clear running. He added for this reason he elected to shift to the inside of Butch’N’Bugs whereby he was able to place his mount under some pressure for a short distance until then being held up from the 300m where he was then obliged to shift to the outside of Butch’N’Bugs and Shaka Rock and furthermore Salsonic to obtain clear running passing the 150m. The Stewards advised B Loy that the better option would have been to shift to the outside of Butch’N’Bugs in the early stages of the straight which would have enabled him to obtain clear running sooner.

title: Appointment Of Steve Railton As Chairman Of Stewards
text: In a career as a Steward spanning 42 years, Steve Railton commenced his career as a Stipendiary Steward in Queensland before being appointed as Chairman of Stewards in 1995. In 2003 he was appointed as Deputy Chairman of Stewards with Racing NSW before accepting a role with the Hong Kong Jockey Club as a Stipendiary Steward and Secretary of the Licensing Committee in 2009, a role he held for 12 years. In 2021 Steve returned to Sydney where he was appointed as Deputy Chairman of Stewards.

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: Racing NSW Stewards today conducted an inquiry into the analyst's finding of caffeine, theophylline and theobromine in a pre-race blood sample taken from Bobby’s Secret prior to it running in Race 8 (Country Boosted Benchmark 58 Handicap, 1300m) at the Dubbo race meeting on 7 March 2025.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: Evidence was taken from Mrs Melissa Harrison, trainer and part-owner of Bobby’s Secret, Australian Racing Forensic Laboratory (ARFL) General Manager Mr John Keledjian and Racing NSW Veterinary Officer Dr Rose Bensley. Stewards also considered a brief of evidence provided by Racing NSW Investigators.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: Background
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: The Stewards established the following:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • On 4 April 2025, Racing NSW Officials notified Mrs Harrison of the irregularity the sample had returned to caffeine and its metabolites theophylline and theobromine. During the associated stable inspection officials took possession of stable treatment records, feed supplements and examined various medications contained within the stable.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • Racing NSW Stewards were, at the time of the stable inspection, aware locally and through liaison with other racing jurisdictions in Australia that the feed supplement Metabolize, which is manufactured by Poseidon Animal Health, had recently been linked to the detection of caffeine.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • An industry Notice was issued by Racing NSW Stewards on 11 March 2025 to all licensed trainers in NSW warning of the identified link between the detection of caffeine and its metabolites in raceday samples with the use of the feed supplement Metabolize
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • It was established during the stable inspection that in the relevant period Mrs Harrison had been providing Metabolize to Bobby’s Secret prior to it racing on 7 March 2025. Ms Harrison, however, immediately ceased using this feed supplement following the warning issued by Racing NSW Stewards on 11 March 2025.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • A sample of Metabolize obtained from Mrs Harrison’s stable and analysed by the Australian Racing Forensic Laboratory was found to contain high levels of caffeine.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • At the inquiry, evidence was tendered from Mr Peter Lord of Poseidon Animal Health that the natural extracts that make up Metabolize do not contain caffeine, however, it had been found that  traces of caffeine had been detected in certain batches of the product manufactured in November 2024. Following a quality control process undertaken by the company, it was identified that the contamination had occurred in the supply of one of the raw materials in the powdered blend and that measures had since been put in place to address the issue.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: Charge
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: Mrs Harrison pleaded guilty to the following offence:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: AR240(2) – Presenting a horse to race with a prohibited substance detected
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: The details of the charge being that she did present Bobby’s Secret to race in the Country Boosted Benchmark 58 Handicap at the Dubbo race meeting on 7 March 2025 and a pre-race blood sample taken from Bobby’s Secret was found to contain the prohibited substances caffeine, theophylline and theobromine.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: Consideration of Penalty
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: In deciding to issue no penalty against Mrs Harrison in relation to the aforementioned breach of AR240(2), consideration was given to the following circumstances:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • That on the evidence, Stewards were satisfied that the source of the detection of caffeine and its metabolites in the sample obtained from Bobby’s Secret resulted from the ingestion of Metabolize which contained caffeine as a consequence of contamination during production.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • Prior to using Metabolize in her racing stable, Mrs Harrison had made appropriate inquiries through a reputable supplier, following which the use of this product had been proposed.

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • Mrs Harrison used Metabolize on the basis that she was aware of other trainers having used the product without issue.

title: Stewards Conclude Inquiry Into Bobby's Secret Irregularity
text: • The product labelling observed by Mrs Harrison, raised no concerns of it containing any prohibited substance and contained no claims in relation the product treating a disease, condition or injury which would require it to be registered with the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicine Authority (APVMA) as required under AR252.

text: • The early entry of a guilty plea.

parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: There is no better example than our current chief Steward Tom Moxon who rose from the traineeship, gained valuable experience working in the country and returned to the Metropolitan panel before being promoted to be Chairman Of Stewards last year at the age of 40.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: It is also well recognised that Stewards who have forged successful careers in New South Wales are keenly sought after internationally which is reflected by those officials who occupy high profile roles in overseas jurisdictions.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: Hong Kong’s panel is headed up by former Racing NSW Chairman of Stewards Marc Van Gestel, who along with colleagues Troy Vassallo and Terry Bailey, commenced his career in NSW, as did Dubai’s chief steward Sam Shinksy.

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: Champion trainer Adrian Bott completed a stewards traineeship from his formative days in the industry while ex-jockeys Andrew Bloomfield and Nick Souquet have recently made the move post their riding careers while also undertaking starting duties.

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: BAXTER BEASLEY – Southern Districts
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: As the son of a jockey, multiple Group 1 winner Danny Beasley, and now trainer it’s not a shock that racing is a huge part of Baxter’s life.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: His first career thoughts were to join the Australian Federal Police but when the opportunity to become one of racing’s ‘police’ came up in early 2023 he jumped at the chance to merge his two passions.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “I’ve always had an interest in integrity and policing roles,” Beasley said.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “There is a lot more to the role than what people see on race day.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “You need to develop a thorough knowledge of the rules, understand investigations, communicate effectively with participants, and make decisions under pressure.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “What surprised me most was the breadth of the role and the amount of preparation and work that happens behind the scenes to maintain the integrity of the industry.”
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: Beasley, 22, is based in the Southern Districts at Wagga. While trainees do have opportunities to preside at city meetings at various times he says starting out in the country has been beneficial.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: In the coming years he aims to join the metropolitan panel and take on the added responsibility that comes with it.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “The traineeship has given me a strong foundation, both technically and professionally, and has exposed me to a wide range of situations that have helped prepare me for the next stage of my career,’’ he said.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “It's provided me with the skills, knowledge, and confidence to continue developing within the industry.”

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: EVIE NORRIS – Metropolitan
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: A racing participant from a young age, Evie has long held a passion for horses and racing and brought a broad understanding of the sport and the people who make it happen with her when she decided to seek out a stewarding career.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: She said what attracted her to the job is the variety it offers and the chance to be involved in race meetings from a different perspective.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “Every race meeting and trial day provides an opportunity to learn something new, and no two days are ever the same,’’ she said.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “The support I've received from the stewards panel and the wider racing industry has made the experience particularly rewarding. Being surrounded by people who are passionate about racing and willing to share their knowledge has made the traineeship both enjoyable and valuable.”
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: Norris, 26, said anybody considering becoming a cadet steward should be aware it requires commitment, attention to detail and a genuine willingness to learn.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: But with it comes the back up of a highly experienced stewards panel, led by Tom Moxon, who are invested in developing and supporting the growth of their trainees.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “Observing how they approach their roles, communicate with industry participants and make decisions has helped me develop both professionally and personally,’’ she said.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “The traineeship has provided an excellent foundation by exposing me to all aspects of the role and giving me opportunities to learn from experienced professionals.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “It has certainly set me up to pursue a long-term career in stewarding and continue contributing to the racing industry.”
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: MARCUS VILO – SERA & Canberra
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: Evie Norris, Marcus Vilo and Baxter Beasley officiating at a recent Hawkesbury meeting. (Pic: Bradley Photos).

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: To become a steward, obviously an interest in horse racing is needed and that’s something that Marcus has developed quickly having not come from a background in racing.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: The road to taking on a traineeship was paved through getting to know some people who are invested in racing and at just 21 years old is now a stipendiary steward.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: He says the position is both challenging and rewarding.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “There is far more to being a steward than what people see on race day,’’ he said.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “What surprised me most was the variety of responsibilities stewards have and the amount of preparation and work that takes place behind the scenes to ensure race meetings run smoothly.”
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: With racing not in his blood, Vilo says it’s been a huge advantage to be able to learn from those above him and it’s a job that continues to throw up new opportunities to grow.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “To have such highly regarded and respected professionals be so approachable and invested in my development is truly a gift for someone in my position,’’ he said.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “The traineeship has provided me with a strong foundation of knowledge and experience. It has equipped me with the skills and confidence needed to continue developing my career.”
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: Racing NSW currently has five trainee stewards. To express interest in joining racing’s integrity department contact Tom Moxon (tmoxon@racingnsw.com.au).
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: All prospective stewards must complete Certificate III in Racing Services, and that takes between one and two years, as part of the traineeship.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: Moxon said in that course you’ll learn all aspects of the role of a Stipendiary Steward and also other race day officials. It’s also important to note that working in regional NSW will be part of the job description.

title: Racing NSW's Next Wave Of Stewards
text: “It is a role where, if you commit yourself to it, you can climb through the ranks really quickly and forge a successful and rewarding career,’’ he said.

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: Racing NSW Stewards have concluded an inquiry into the conduct of licensed jockey Mikayla Weir in the scales area at Gunnedah Race Club following the running of Race 1 on 15 August 2023.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: Stewards considered a brief of evidence prepared by Racing NSW Investigator N. Bourke as well as evidence from Mikayla Weir and apprentice jockey Lachlan Scorse who was assisted by Mr Corey Brown-Racing NSW Head Apprentice Jockey Coach.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: After the consideration of all the evidence, Mikayla Weir was issued the following charge under AR228(b):
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: AR 228 Conduct detrimental to the interests of racing
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: A person must not engage in:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: (b) misconduct, improper conduct or unseemly behaviour;
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: The particulars of the charge being that:
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: When present in the scales area following the running of Race 1 at the Gunnedah race meeting on 15 August 2023, whilst in view and earshot of the public and other industry participants, she did engage in misconduct by directing comments to, and or making comments about apprentice Lachlan Scorse that were improper.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: Plea: Guilty
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: Stewards considered the following
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: Stewards considered the following matters when assessing penalty –
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: 1. Nature of the offence & the explanation offered.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: 2. Mikayla Weir’s record in relation to conduct-related matters
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: 3. Personal and professional circumstances.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: 4. Apprentice Lachlan Scorse’s inexperience in the racing industry and the effect such incidents may have on inexperienced apprentice jockeys.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: 5. The fact that the incident occurred whilst in the view of and earshot of industry participants and the public.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: 6. Principle of specific and general deterrence and what message is to be sent to the industry with respect to such conduct.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: 7. Purpose for issuing penalties as a protective measure for the image and integrity of the thoroughbred Industry.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: Stewards determined that the appropriate penalty be a 2-week suspension of Ms Weir’s license to ride in races.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: However, having regard to the mitigating factors, Stewards, acting under the powers of AR283(5) suspended 1 week of the penalty for a period of 2 years on the condition Ms Weir does not breach any conduct-related rules at that time.
parse_note: not tied to a race and horse

title: Racing NSW Stewards Suspend And Fine Licensed Jockey Mikayla Weir
text: Such suspension is to commence on Wednesday, 13 September 2023 and expire on Wednesday, 20 September 2023, on which day she may ride.
